source.spoken_script: An old man in the temple held a baby and told the mother one dark sentence. Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also. Simeon told Mary. Some thirty years later, the sword lands. Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother. Close enough to watch her son die. Jesus looks down, sees her wound, and turns to bind it. When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son! Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home. He gave her the disciple he loved. A son. A home. While judgment fell on him, he cared for someone else. That is who is dying there. Your wound is not invisible to him. He sees it from the cross. Stand where Mary stood. The Son who saw her will behold you, and bind what the sword tore.

platforms.title: While Dying, He Arranged His Mother's Care
platforms.description:
At the cross (John 19:26), a thirty-year-old sentence finally lands.

When Mary carried her baby into the temple, old Simeon told her one dark thing: a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also. Now she stands close enough to watch her son die. The sword has landed.

And Jesus looks down, sees her wound, and turns to bind it: "When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!" (John 19:26, KJV). Then to the disciple: behold thy mother. And from that hour, John took her into his own home.

While judgment fell on him, he cared for someone else. That is who is dying there.

Your wound is not invisible to him either. Stand where Mary stood. The Son who saw her will behold you, and bind what the sword tore.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Woman, Behold Thy Son: The Sword That Landed at the Cross
platforms.description:
Thirty years before the cross (John 19:26), an old man in the temple held a newborn and told the mother one dark sentence: "Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also" (Luke 2:35).

Simeon said it to Mary. And at Golgotha, the sword lands: "Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother." Close enough to watch her son die.

Then the third Word from the cross: "When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!" (John 19:26, KJV). Then to John: behold thy mother. And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.

In the very hour judgment fell on him, Jesus saw one grieving woman, and arranged a son and a home for her. He did not manage his own agony first. He bound her wound from inside his own.

In this piece: Simeon's sword and its thirty-year arc, Mary standing at the cross, why Jesus entrusted her to the disciple he loved, and what the scene says about how he sees the wounded now.

Your wound is not invisible to him. Stand where Mary stood. The Son who saw her will behold you, and bind what the sword tore.

VERDICT: PASS

- Verbatim: the John 19:26 anchor is character-exact everywhere quoted. The Simeon
  line "Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also" is quoted with its Luke
  2:35 ref in the long description and rendered unquoted-paraphrase elsewhere - clean.
- Ref front-load: "(John 19:26)" appears inside the first 157 chars of youtube_short
  and youtube_long; facebook opens with "(Luke 2:35)" then carries John 19:26 - the
  anchor ref 'john' also appears within the fold via the verse cite. Clean.
- Typography: all-ASCII. Clean.
- Doctrine: "he bound her wound from inside his own" is vivid but faithful to the
  scene; no Marian overclaim (no mediation language, no veneration) - the CTA lands
  on the SON beholding the viewer, which is the video's landing. Grace-anchored.
- Titles: "While Dying, He Arranged His Mother's Care" - true, understated, strong.
  "The Word Nobody Preaches On" (candidate 3) borders on rhetorical inflation but is
  NOT the chosen title. Chosen set is clean.
- Nothing blocking.
